title: Uniform Random Example Bound
statement: For all natural numbers $n,k,b$, the maximum, over all subsets $P\subseteq[n]$, of the node's random-example count at failure parameter $\delta_{k,b}$ is at most $A_k(n+1)^{\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor+3}(b+1)$. Here $T_0=1$, $T_{j+1}=1+2T_j$, $c_k=\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$, $d_k=k-c_k$, $L_k=\lceil\log_2 T_k\rceil+2(c_k+1)+5$, and $A_k=2^{k+1}B_k+16\cdot4^kL_k$, where $B_k=(c_k+1)(36\cdot4^kL_k)+2^{d_k}(d_k+1+L_k)$. The parameter is $\delta_{k,b}=(1/T_k)2^{-(b+1)}$, and the random-example count for a fixed $P$ is the restriction sample count with failure parameter $\delta_{k,b}/2$.
hypotheses_covered: the bound holds uniformly over all subsets $P\subseteq[n]
the failure parameter is the specified dyadic per-call failure parameter
